title: How the liver can regrow itself

explain.say: The liver is the only internal organ in people that can regrow to its full size after a large part of it has been removed. Even with only about a third left, it can grow back.

explain.say: When part of the liver is lost, the remaining liver cells, which normally rarely divide, switch on and start dividing quickly. Signals in the blood tell them that the liver is too small.

explain.say: The liver regrows its size and its ability to work, though not its exact original shape: the remaining parts swell larger. Most of the size returns within a few weeks to months.

explain.say: Once the liver reaches the right size for the body, the cells stop dividing. This is why a living person can donate part of their liver, and both pieces grow into working livers.

faq.q: Can the liver really grow back?
faq.a: Yes. If part of the liver is removed, the rest can regrow to about its original size and work normally. It can recover even when only about a third remains.
asks: How much of the liver can grow back?
Is it true the liver regenerates?

faq.a: Liver cells, called hepatocytes, normally divide rarely. When the liver loses tissue, signals switch them back on and they divide until the liver is the right size again.

faq.q: Does the liver grow back in its original shape?
faq.a: Not exactly. The removed lobes do not reappear; instead the remaining lobes grow larger. The liver regains its size and function rather than its exact shape.
asks: Does the liver regrow the same shape?
What does a regrown liver look like?

faq.q: How does the liver know when to stop growing?
faq.a: The liver seems to sense its size relative to the body's needs. Once it is big enough, growth signals fade and stopping signals take over, so the cells stop dividing.
asks: Why does the liver stop regrowing?
How does an organ know its size?

faq.q: Why can someone donate part of their liver?
faq.a: Because both the donor's remaining liver and the transplanted piece can regrow, a living donor can give part of their liver and both people end up with working livers.
asks: How does a living liver donation work?
Can you give away part of your liver?

facts: The liver can regenerate even after about two thirds of it has been removed.
The ancient Greek myth of Prometheus describes an eagle eating his liver, which grew back each day.
